questions.question: Grammar: E→E1+T {E.val=E1.val+T.val} | T {E.val=T.val}; T→num {T.val=num.val}. Compute E.val for input '3+4+5'.
questions.solutionApproach: Left-associative: parse as (3+4)+5. T.val=3 for first num. E→T gives E.val=3. Then E1+T: E.val=3+4=7. Then E1+T: E.val=7+5=12.

questions.question: A→BC with rules: B.inh = A.inh (inherited, from parent), C.inh = B.syn (inherited, from LEFT sibling B). Is this SDD L-attributed?
questions.solutionApproach: B.inh depends on A.inh (parent) — fine. C.inh depends on B.syn (a sibling to its LEFT) — fine, left-dependency allowed. No right-dependencies found. This IS L-attributed.
questions.answer: Yes, L-attributed — all inherited attributes depend only on parent or left siblings.

questions.question: A→BC with rule: B.inh = C.syn (B's inherited attribute depends on C, which is to B's RIGHT). Is this L-attributed? Can a bottom-up parser evaluate it?
questions.solutionApproach: B.inh depends on C.syn — C is to the RIGHT of B in the production. This violates the L-attributed left-only-dependency rule. NOT L-attributed. Therefore a bottom-up (LR) parser CANNOT evaluate this inherited attribute during normal single-pass parsing.
questions.answer: No, not L-attributed (right-dependency) — cannot be evaluated during bottom-up parsing.
